criteria.text: The response identifies that, under SPA Sections 8.1 and 8.2(c), Buyer's Pre-Closing Tax indemnity in effect lapses about six months after Closing because it is tied to the six-month survival period, long before pre-closing taxes are likely to be assessed. It explains why this matters to Rilux and recommends a fix.
hints: six months following the Closing Date

criteria.text: The response identifies that Bill of Sale Section 5 requires the Company to indemnify Seller, without any cap, for all liabilities relating to the Conveyed Assets, including pre-closing liabilities, and that the SPA does not limit this indemnity. It explains why this matters to Rilux and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that Seller's license-back under IP Assignment Agreement Sections 4 and 9.3 is freely transferable, so Seller could pass the SORRELFIELD brand and recipe rights to a competitor that the SPA non-compete does not bind. It explains why this matters to Rilux and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that the Ashbourne Valley Cooperative's change-of-control consent under the Raw Organic Milk Supply Agreement was not obtained for the sale, leaving the Cooperative able to terminate the Company's milk supply. It locates the issue in the SPA (Disclosure Schedule 4.5(a), Section 6.4 or Section 7.2(d)), explains why this matters to Rilux and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that Buyer's June 12, 2026 Notice of Disagreement fell outside the 30-day window under SPA Section 2.4(b), which closed on May 30, 2026 after the April 30, 2026 Closing Statement, so on the face of the SPA Seller's Closing Statement is final and binding. It explains why this matters to Rilux and recommends a fix.
The response states that the Closing Date was April 1, 2026.
The response is structured as a memo to the supervising partner. Each issue is presented separately and gives the document and section, why the issue matters, and a recommended fix.
The response presents the issues in an order of significance, with the most consequential items first or expressly ranked by priority.
The response claims that Buyer's June 12, 2026 Notice of Disagreement was timely under SPA Section 2.4(b).
The response claims that the SPA Section 8.6 cap limits the Company's indemnity of Seller under Bill of Sale Section 5.
